newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end higher, aided by oils.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end higher, aided by oils.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended stronger on Monday, spurred by surging oils and a growing belief that the U.S. Federal Reserve will refrain from hiking short-term interest rates at its May 20 meeting.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index jumped 43.27 points to 6272.58. Turnover totalled 97.8 million shares worth C$1.5 billion ($1.1 billion).
"If the Fed doesn't get too anxious on ... May 20, then this market will be seen as good value," said Dunnery Best, director of private client investing at Midland Walwyn.

Toronto's influential oil and gas sector benefited from rising energy prices, Best said. June crude oil futures on NYMEX ended up $0.95 at $21.38, helped by news of earthquakes in two major oil exporting countries: Iran and Colombia.
All but three of Toronto's 14 sub-indices -- golds, pipelines and real estate -- ticked higher. Consumer products, oils, transportation and base metals led the march upward.
The market is closing in on its all-time high of 6348.02 points, set March 11.
Advancing issues outstripped decliners 601 to 391 while 298 ended steady.
In individual issues, Berkley Petroleum Corp. climbed 2.55 to 36.50 while Talisman Energy Inc. rose 1.70 to 44.70.
Pure Gold Resources Inc. bucked the trend for falling golds and rose 0.04 to 0.53 on nearly 7.6 shares, topping most actives in Toronto.
Banks continued to roll higher. Bank of Nova Scotia, Canada's fourth largest, added 1.05 to hit 56.60.
